Medicine 06.question: ১) Which is a life saving drug in acute pulmonary oedema?
Medicine 06.exp:
Frusemide (furosemide) is a key life-saving drug in acute pulmonary oedema, particularly when due to acute left ventricular failure. It produces rapid diuresis, reducing intravascular volume and pulmonary congestion.

  • Frusemide → potent loop diuretic → reduces pulmonary edema

  • GTN → reduces preload/afterload and is very useful, especially with severe hypertension

  • Thiazides → not suitable for acute pulmonary edema

  • Opiates → not routinely recommended

Exam pearl:
“Acute pulmonary oedema → IV frusemide.”

Medicine 06.question: ২) Which one is a feature of type-2 DM?
Medicine 06.option2: rapid death without treatment with insulin
Medicine 06.exp:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) has a strong genetic/familial predisposition, so a family history of diabetes is common.

  • Type 2 DM → family history commonly present

  • Body weight → often overweight/obese, rather than normal or low

  • Insulin is not usually immediately life-saving in untreated T2DM

  • Typical onset → usually ≥40 years, although it can occur at younger ages

Exam pearl:
“Type 2 DM → strong family history + obesity/insulin resistance.”

Medicine 06.question: ৩) Which disease follow rule of ten?
Medicine 06.exp:
Pheochromocytoma is classically associated with the “Rule of 10s” in traditional teaching:

  • 10% bilateral

  • 10% extra-adrenal (paraganglioma)

  • 10% malignant

  • 10% occur in children

  • 10% familial

  • 10% may be asymptomatic

Modern studies show these percentages are not exact, but the Rule of 10s remains a common exam concept.

Exam pearl:
“Rule of 10s → Pheochromocytoma.”

Medicine 06.question: ৪) The risk of developing type-2 DM increases tenfold in a people with a BMI >....... kg/m2?
Medicine 06.exp:
The risk of developing type 2 diabetes mellitus increases markedly with increasing obesity. A BMI >30 kg/m² (obesity) is classically associated with approximately a 10-fold increased risk compared with normal BMI.

BMI classification:

  • 18.5–24.9 → Normal

  • 25–29.9 → Overweight

  • ≥30 → Obesity

Exam pearl:
“BMI >30 kg/m² → ~10× increased risk of type 2 DM.”

Medicine 06.question: ৫) Criterias of acute severe bronchial asthma excludes...?
Medicine 06.option1: inability to complete a sentence in one breath
Medicine 06.option2: RR more than or equal to 35/min
Medicine 06.option3: tachycardia more than or equal to 110 / min
Medicine 06.exp:
In acute severe bronchial asthma, commonly used clinical criteria include:

  • Inability to complete sentences in one breath

  • Pulse rate ≥110/min

  • Respiratory rate ≥25/min

  • PEFR 33–50% of predicted/best

Therefore, RR ≥35/min is not the standard criterion; the conventional cutoff is ≥25/min.

Exam pearl:
Acute severe asthma → RR ≥25/min + pulse ≥110/min + PEFR 33–50% + unable to complete sentences.

Medicine 06.question: ৬) Which disease is diagnosed by water deprivation test?
Medicine 06.exp:
The water deprivation test is used to evaluate polyuria and suspected diabetes insipidus (DI). It helps distinguish:

  • Central DI → responds to desmopressin (DDAVP)

  • Nephrogenic DI → little or no response to desmopressin

  • Primary polydipsia → urine concentration improves during water deprivation

Exam pearl:
“Water deprivation test → Diabetes insipidus.”

Medicine 06.question: ৭) Which one is not pathophysiology of Type-2 DM?
Medicine 06.option4: elevated plasma glucose & free fatty acids
Medicine 06.exp:
The main pathophysiological features of Type 2 diabetes mellitus include:

  • Insulin resistance → decreased response of tissues to insulin

  • β-cell dysfunction/failure → progressive reduction in insulin secretion

  • Elevated plasma glucose and free fatty acids → contribute to glucotoxicity and lipotoxicity

Insulitis (inflammatory destruction of pancreatic β-cells) is classically associated with Type 1 diabetes mellitus, not Type 2 DM.

Exam pearl:
“Type 1 → Insulitis; Type 2 → Insulin resistance + β-cell failure.”

Medicine 06.question: ৮) Which is not true about acromegaly?
Medicine 06.exp:
Acromegaly occurs due to excess growth hormone (GH) after epiphyseal plates have fused. Therefore, height does not increase; instead, there is enlargement of the hands, feet, jaw, and facial bones.

  • Height increased → false in acromegaly

  • Hands and feet enlarged → true

  • Protruding lower jaw (prognathism) → true

  • Kyphosis → may occur due to skeletal changes

High-yield recall:
Before epiphyseal closure → Gigantism → ↑ height
After epiphyseal closure → Acromegaly → ↑ bone/soft-tissue thickness, not height

Exam pearl:
“Acromegaly = increased size, not increased height.”

Medicine 06.question: ৯) What is the significance of following blood glucose level? FBS : <7.0 mmol/L & 2hrs ABF : 7.8 -11.0 mmol/L
Medicine 06.exp:
The 2-hour post-glucose/ABF value of 7.8–11.0 mmol/L indicates Impaired Glucose Tolerance (IGT) when the fasting glucose is below the diabetic range.

Diagnostic ranges:

  • Normal: 2-hour glucose <7.8 mmol/L

  • IGT: 2-hour glucose 7.8–11.0 mmol/L

  • Diabetes mellitus: 2-hour glucose ≥11.1 mmol/L

Exam pearl:
“2-hour glucose 7.8–11.0 mmol/L → IGT.”

Medicine 06.question: ১০) In hypertensive emergency BP should not be reduced more than....... % in 1st hour?
Medicine 06.exp:
In a hypertensive emergency, BP should be lowered carefully and gradually to avoid reducing blood flow to vital organs.

  • First hour → reduce MAP/BP by no more than ~25%

  • Then, if stable, reduce to approximately 160/100–110 mmHg over the next 2–6 hours

  • Further gradual reduction over the following 24–48 hours

Why not rapid reduction?
A sudden fall in BP can cause cerebral, coronary, or renal ischemia.

Exam pearl:
“Hypertensive emergency → ↓ BP ≤25% in the first hour.”

Medicine 06.question: ১১) Which symptom is not due to neuropathy in diabetic foot?
Medicine 06.exp:
Claudication is a symptom of peripheral arterial disease (vascular insufficiency), not diabetic neuropathy.

Neuropathy commonly causes:

  • Paresthesia

  • Pain (especially burning pain)

  • Numbness

  • Loss of protective sensation

Claudication → typically muscle pain on walking due to inadequate arterial blood flow.

Exam pearl:
“Neuropathy → numbness/paresthesia; PAD → claudication.”

Medicine 06.question: ১২) What is the target BP of a diabetic patient with proteinuria >1g/24hrs?
Medicine 06.exp:
In traditional exam-based guidelines, a diabetic patient with significant proteinuria (>1 g/24 h) has a lower target BP of approximately 125/75 mmHg to reduce progression of diabetic nephropathy.

  • Proteinuria >1 g/day → target BP ≈ 125/75 mmHg

  • More aggressive BP control helps reduce proteinuria and renal disease progression.

Exam pearl:
“Diabetes + proteinuria >1 g/day → BP target 125/75 mmHg.”

Medicine 06.question: ১৩) Which is feature of diabetic retinopathy?
Medicine 06.exp:
Dot-and-blot hemorrhages are characteristic of diabetic retinopathy, particularly background/non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy (NPDR). They arise from bleeding of the deeper retinal capillary layers.

  • Dot & blot hemorrhage → Diabetic retinopathy

  • Flame-shaped hemorrhage → typically hypertensive retinopathy

  • Silver wiring → hypertensive retinopathy

  • Papilloedema → raised intracranial pressure

Exam pearl:
“Diabetic retinopathy → dot-and-blot hemorrhages + microaneurysms.”

Medicine 06.question: ১৪) What is the cause of maximum percentage of deaths in a people with DM?
Medicine 06.exp:
Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death among people with diabetes mellitus. Chronic hyperglycemia accelerates atherosclerosis, increasing the risk of:

  • Myocardial infarction

  • Stroke

  • Peripheral arterial disease

  • Heart failure

Exam pearl:
“Diabetes → most deaths are due to cardiovascular disease.”

Medicine 06.question: ১৫) Longer term anticonvulsant medication after control of status epilepticus excludes.....?
Medicine 06.exp:
After status epilepticus is controlled, longer-term antiseizure therapy may include drugs such as:

  • Sodium valproate

  • Phenytoin

  • Carbamazepine

Diazepam is a benzodiazepine used for acute seizure termination, but it is not generally used as long-term maintenance therapy because of tolerance, sedation, and dependence.

Exam pearl:
“Status epilepticus → Diazepam for acute control; not for long-term maintenance.”

Medicine 06.question: ১৬) If you fail to differentiate between hypoglycemic coma & hyperglycemic coma then what you'll treat empirically?
Medicine 06.exp:
If it is not possible to immediately differentiate between hypoglycemic coma and hyperglycemic coma, hypoglycemia should be treated empirically with glucose (dextrose) because untreated hypoglycemia can rapidly cause irreversible brain injury or death.

  • Hypoglycemia → immediate glucose

  • Hyperglycemic coma requires different treatment and should be confirmed with blood glucose testing when possible.

Exam pearl:
“Uncertain diabetic coma → give glucose first if hypoglycemia cannot be excluded.”

Medicine 06.question: ১৭) Which oral antidiabetic drug is incretin mimetics?
Medicine 06.exp:
Sitagliptin is a DPP-4 inhibitor, which works by preventing the breakdown of endogenous incretin hormones (GLP-1 and GIP). This enhances glucose-dependent insulin secretion and suppresses glucagon release.

Strictly speaking, sitagliptin is an incretin enhancer, not an incretin mimetic. True incretin mimetics are GLP-1 receptor agonists such as exenatide and liraglutide.

For this MCQ, the intended answer is sitagliptin.

Exam pearl:
“Sitagliptin = DPP-4 inhibitor → incretin effect.”

Medicine 06.question: ১৮) What is the blood glucose level (mmol/L) in hypoglycemia?
Medicine 06.exp:
In conventional clinical/exam definitions, hypoglycemia is a blood glucose level <3.5 mmol/L.

  • <3.5 mmol/L → Hypoglycemia

  • Symptoms may include sweating, tremor, hunger, palpitations, confusion, and seizures.

  • Severe/prolonged hypoglycemia can lead to coma.

Exam pearl:
“Hypoglycemia → blood glucose <3.5 mmol/L.”

Medicine 06.question: ১৯) Which insulin preparation is long acting?
Medicine 06.exp:
Insulin glargine is a long-acting basal insulin with a relatively prolonged, nearly peakless action.

  • Aspart → rapid-acting

  • Isophane (NPH) → intermediate-acting

  • Ultralente → long-acting, but it is an older preparation and is no longer commonly used

  • Glargine → long-acting

Exam pearl:
“Glargine = long-acting basal insulin.”

Medicine 06.question: ২০) Which MI is worst?
Medicine 06.exp:
Anterior myocardial infarction (MI) is generally considered the worst/prognostically most serious because it usually involves a larger area of myocardium, often due to left anterior descending (LAD) coronary artery occlusion.

  • Anterior MI → large infarct size, higher risk of LV failure, cardiogenic shock, and mortality

  • Inferior MI → often due to RCA occlusion

  • Lateral MI → usually smaller territory

  • Septal MI → involves interventricular septum

Exam pearl:
“Worst prognosis among common MI locations → Anterior MI.”

Medicine 06.question: ২১) In a DKA patient if potassium level is from 3.5 to 5.5 mmol/L then...... mmol of potassium is to be added in per litre of infusion?
Medicine 06.exp:
In DKA, total body potassium is usually depleted even when the initial serum K⁺ is normal or high.

If serum K⁺ = 3.5–5.5 mmol/L, potassium replacement is typically added to IV fluid at about 40 mmol/L, provided the patient is producing urine and there is no significant hyperkalemia.

  • K⁺ <3.5 mmol/L → replace K⁺ first and delay insulin

  • K⁺ 3.5–5.5 mmol/L → add K⁺ to IV fluids

  • K⁺ >5.5 mmol/L → initially withhold K⁺ and monitor

Exam pearl:
“DKA + K⁺ 3.5–5.5 mmol/L → add 40 mmol K⁺/L.”

Medicine 06.question: ২২) Which is a microvascular complication of DM?
Medicine 06.exp:
Diabetic neuropathy is a microvascular complication of diabetes mellitus, resulting from chronic hyperglycemia and associated metabolic/microvascular injury.

Major microvascular complications:

  • Retinopathy

  • Nephropathy

  • Neuropathy

Whereas:

  • Stroke → macrovascular complication

  • MI → macrovascular complication

  • DKA → acute metabolic complication

Exam pearl:
“DM microvascular triad = Retinopathy + Nephropathy + Neuropathy.”

Medicine 06.question: ২৩) What is the significant side effect of insulin therapy?
Medicine 06.exp:
The most significant and potentially dangerous side effect of insulin therapy is hypoglycemia. It occurs when the amount of insulin exceeds the body's current glucose requirement.

Common features:

  • Sweating

  • Tremor

  • Palpitations

  • Hunger

  • Confusion

  • Seizures or coma in severe cases

Other effects: Weight gain and peripheral edema can occur, but hypoglycemia is the major clinically important adverse effect.

Exam pearl:
“Insulin therapy → most important adverse effect = Hypoglycemia.”

Medicine 06.question: ২৪) Which is not a cardinal biochemical features of DKA?
Medicine 06.exp:
The cardinal biochemical features of DKA are:

  • Hyperglycemia

  • Hyperketonemia/ketonuria

  • Metabolic acidosis (high anion gap)

Although the serum K⁺ may be normal or even elevated initially, the patient actually has total-body potassium depletion due to osmotic diuresis and urinary losses. Therefore, hyperkalemia is not a cardinal biochemical feature of DKA.

Exam pearl:
DKA = Hyperglycemia + Ketosis + Metabolic acidosis.

Medicine 06.question: ২৫) What is the most dangerous complication of MI?
Medicine 06.exp:
Ventricular fibrillation (VF) is one of the most dangerous complications of acute myocardial infarction (MI) because it causes immediate loss of effective cardiac output and can lead to sudden cardiac death within minutes if not treated.

  • Ventricular fibrillation → life-threatening arrhythmia

  • Atrial fibrillation → usually less immediately fatal

  • Pericarditis → recognized complication, but not the most immediately dangerous

  • Cardiac remodeling → long-term complication

Exam pearl:
“MI + sudden collapse → think ventricular fibrillation.”

Medicine 06.question: ২৬) What is the average amount of sodium loss in an adult patient of DKA with moderate severity?
Medicine 06.exp:
In a moderate DKA, there is significant total-body sodium depletion due to osmotic diuresis, vomiting, and urinary electrolyte loss. The average sodium deficit in an adult is approximately 500 mmol.

  • Moderate DKA → Na⁺ loss ≈ 500 mmol

  • This contributes to dehydration and reduced circulating volume.

  • Fluid replacement with isotonic saline is an important initial treatment.

Exam pearl:
“Moderate DKA → average sodium loss ≈ 500 mmol.”

Medicine 06.question: ২৭) Hypothyroidism leads to......... in adults?
Medicine 06.exp:
Hypothyroidism in adults causes myxoedema, characterized by features such as fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance, dry skin, constipation, and non-pitting edema.

  • Adult hypothyroidism → Myxoedema

  • Childhood hypothyroidism → Cretinism

  • Exophthalmos → Graves’ disease (hyperthyroidism)

  • Goiter → may occur in some thyroid disorders but is not synonymous with hypothyroidism

Exam pearl:
“Adult hypothyroidism = Myxoedema; childhood hypothyroidism = Cretinism.”

Medicine 06.question: ২৮) Which is the feature of DKA?
Medicine 06.exp:
Kussmaul's breathing is a characteristic feature of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). It is deep, rapid breathing that develops as the body attempts to compensate for metabolic acidosis by eliminating CO₂.

  • Kussmaul's breathing → DKA

  • Sweating → more typical of hypoglycemia

  • Cold periphery → may occur in severe shock/dehydration, but not a defining feature

  • Bounding pulse → not typical of DKA

Exam pearl:
“DKA → deep, rapid Kussmaul breathing.”

Medicine 06.question: ২৯) Failure of adrenal cortex to secrete corticosteroids is known as......?
Medicine 06.exp:
Addison disease (primary adrenal insufficiency) occurs when the adrenal cortex fails to produce adequate corticosteroid hormones, especially cortisol and often aldosterone.

  • Addison disease → ↓ cortisol + ↓ aldosterone

  • Cushing syndrome → excess cortisol

  • Adrenogenital syndrome → excess adrenal androgens

  • Pseudohermaphroditism → abnormal sexual development

Exam pearl:
“Adrenal cortex failure → Addison disease.”

Medicine 06.question: ৩০) Which is not an early complication of drowning?
Medicine 06.exp:
Dehydration is not an early complication of drowning. Drowning primarily causes hypoxia due to respiratory impairment and aspiration.

Early complications/signs may include:

  • Pulmonary edema

  • Hypotension/shock

  • Hemoptysis due to airway/lung injury

  • Hypoxemia and respiratory distress

Exam pearl:
“Drowning → aspiration + hypoxia + pulmonary edema; dehydration is not a typical early complication.”

Medicine 06.question: ৩১) What is the feature of somatic neuropathy?
Medicine 06.exp:
Somatic neuropathy affects motor and sensory nerves, producing muscle weakness, wasting, numbness, and loss of sensation.

  • Small muscle wasting → somatic motor neuropathy

  • Gustatory sweating → autonomic neuropathy

  • Postural hypotension → autonomic neuropathy

  • Erectile dysfunction → autonomic neuropathy

Exam pearl:
“Somatic neuropathy → sensory loss + muscle weakness/wasting.”

Medicine 06.question: ৩২) What is not a cause of thyroid overactivity?
Medicine 06.exp:
Cretinism is a condition caused by severe congenital/childhood hypothyroidism, so it does not cause thyroid overactivity.

  • Graves' disease → hyperthyroidism

  • Toxic goiter → hyperthyroidism

  • Hashimoto's thyroiditis → usually hypothyroidism, though it can cause a transient hyperthyroid phase (Hashitoxicosis)

  • Cretinism → hypothyroidism

Exam pearl:
“Cretinism = congenital hypothyroidism, not thyroid overactivity.”

Medicine 06.question: ৩৩) Which endocrine gland is not controlled by pituitary gland?
Medicine 06.exp:
The parathyroid gland is not under direct pituitary control. Its secretion of parathyroid hormone (PTH) is primarily regulated by the serum ionized calcium level.

  • Thyroid → TSH from anterior pituitary

  • Adrenal cortex → ACTH from anterior pituitary

  • Ovary → FSH & LH from anterior pituitary

  • Parathyroid → mainly regulated by serum Ca²⁺

Exam pearl:
“Parathyroid = calcium-controlled, not pituitary-controlled.”

Medicine 06.question: ৩৪) Hypersecretion of growth hormone after the union of epiphysis & diaphysis results in.......?
Medicine 06.exp:
If growth hormone (GH) is hypersecreted after fusion of the epiphyseal plates (epiphysis and diaphysis), the long bones can no longer increase in length. Instead, there is thickening/enlargement of bones and soft tissues, producing acromegaly.

  • After epiphyseal fusion + ↑ GH → Acromegaly

  • Before epiphyseal fusion + ↑ GH → Gigantism

  • Dwarfism → inadequate growth hormone/other causes

  • Cretinism → childhood hypothyroidism

Exam pearl:
“GH excess after epiphyseal closure = Acromegaly.”

Medicine 06.question: ৩৫) Which sign is not suitable with hepatic encephalopathy?
Medicine 06.exp:
Hepatic encephalopathy is a neuropsychiatric syndrome caused by liver dysfunction and accumulation of neurotoxins such as ammonia.

Typical findings include:

  • Asterixis (flapping tremor)

  • Constructional apraxia

  • Fetor hepaticus

  • Altered consciousness and confusion

  • Extensor plantar response (Babinski sign) may occur in severe cases

Bilateral plantar flexion is not a typical neurological sign of hepatic encephalopathy. The expected abnormal plantar response, when present, is extension (dorsiflexion) of the great toe, not flexion.

Exam pearl:
“Hepatic encephalopathy → asterixis + constructional apraxia + fetor hepaticus.”

Medicine 06.question: ৩৬) Endocrine cause of weight loss excludes.....?
Medicine 06.exp:
Type 2 diabetes mellitus is not a classic endocrine cause of unexplained weight loss; patients are often overweight or obese due to insulin resistance.

Common endocrine causes of weight loss include:

  • Thyrotoxicosis → ↑ metabolic rate → weight loss

  • Addison's disease → ↓ appetite + cortisol deficiency → weight loss

  • Type 1 DM → insulin deficiency → fat/protein breakdown → weight loss

  • Type 2 DM → usually associated with overweight/obesity

Exam pearl:
“Endocrine weight loss → Thyrotoxicosis + Addison’s + Type 1 DM.”

Medicine 06.question: ৩৭) Pheochromocytoma is a condition characterized by hypersecretion of.........?
Medicine 06.exp:
Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secreting tumor arising from chromaffin cells, usually in the adrenal medulla.

It causes excess:

  • Adrenaline (epinephrine)

  • Noradrenaline (norepinephrine)

  • Sometimes dopamine

Typical clinical features include episodic headache, sweating, palpitations, and hypertension.

Exam pearl:
“Pheochromocytoma → excess catecholamines from adrenal medulla.”

Medicine 06.question: ৩৮) Thyroid hormone excess doesn't happen in which disease?
Medicine 06.exp:
Hashimoto's thyroiditis is primarily an autoimmune hypothyroid disorder, characterized by progressive destruction of thyroid follicles and reduced thyroid hormone production.

  • Graves' disease → thyroid hormone excess

  • Multinodular toxic goiter → thyroid hormone excess

  • Subacute (De Quervain) thyroiditis → transient thyroid hormone excess due to release of preformed hormones

  • Hashimoto's thyroiditis → usually hypothyroidism

Exam pearl:
“Thyroid hormone excess → Graves + toxic multinodular goiter + subacute thyroiditis; Hashimoto’s usually causes hypothyroidism.”

Medicine 06.question: ৩৯) Which one is not a feature of hyperthyroidism?
Medicine 06.exp:
Hyperthyroidism increases basal metabolic rate, so patients typically have weight loss despite increased appetite.

  • Excitability → common

  • Weight gain → not typical; weight loss is expected

  • Muscle weakness → common

  • Heat intolerance → common

Exam pearl:
“Hyperthyroidism → weight loss + heat intolerance + increased excitability.”

Medicine 06.question: ৪০) What is the commonest cause of upper GIT bleeding?
Medicine 06.exp:
Peptic ulcer disease (PUD) is the commonest cause of upper gastrointestinal (UGI) bleeding.

Common causes include:

  • Bleeding PUD → most common

  • Gastric/duodenal erosions

  • Esophagitis

  • Esophageal varices

  • Vascular lesions

Exam pearl:
“Most common cause of upper GI bleeding = Peptic ulcer disease.”

Medicine 06.question: ৪১) Any age with large goiter, poor drug compliance & recurrent thyrotoxicosis demands......?
Medicine 06.exp:
A patient with large goiter, poor compliance with antithyroid drugs, and recurrent thyrotoxicosis is a classic indication for surgical treatment.

Among the given options, the traditional exam answer is subtotal thyroidectomy.

  • Large goiter → surgery preferred

  • Poor drug compliance → long-term medical therapy is unsuitable

  • Recurrent thyrotoxicosis → definitive treatment required

  • Subtotal thyroidectomy → traditional surgical option

Exam pearl:
“Large goiter + recurrent thyrotoxicosis + poor compliance → thyroidectomy.”

Medicine 06.question: ৪২) Dexamethasone suppression test is an investigation for.....?
Medicine 06.exp:
The dexamethasone suppression test (DST) is used to investigate Cushing's syndrome. Dexamethasone is a potent glucocorticoid that normally suppresses ACTH secretion and therefore lowers cortisol production.

  • Cushing's syndrome → failure to appropriately suppress cortisol with dexamethasone

  • Addison's disease → diagnosed mainly by cortisol/ACTH testing and ACTH stimulation test

  • Conn's syndrome → evaluated with aldosterone-renin ratio

Exam pearl:
“Dexamethasone suppression test → Cushing's syndrome.”

Medicine 06.question: ৪৩) Which is the commonest drug used in hyperthyroidism?
Medicine 06.exp:
Carbimazole is the commonly used antithyroid drug for hyperthyroidism, particularly in the UK and many other settings. It is a prodrug of methimazole and inhibits thyroid hormone synthesis.

  • Carbimazole → commonly used antithyroid drug

  • Methimazole → active metabolite of carbimazole

  • PTU → mainly preferred in specific situations, such as the 1st trimester of pregnancy or thyroid storm

  • Propranolol → controls adrenergic symptoms but does not reduce thyroid hormone synthesis

Exam pearl:
“Commonly used antithyroid drug → Carbimazole.”

Medicine 06.question: ৪৪) A patient receiving carbimazole comes to you with sore throat. what may be the reason?
Medicine 06.exp:
Carbimazole can rarely cause agranulocytosis, a potentially life-threatening reduction in neutrophils. A patient taking carbimazole who develops sore throat, fever, or mouth ulcers should be suspected of having agranulocytosis.

What to do:
Stop carbimazole and urgently check a CBC with differential/absolute neutrophil count.

  • Agranulocytosis → sore throat + fever → important warning sign

  • It is a rare but serious adverse effect of antithyroid drugs.

Exam pearl:
“Carbimazole + sore throat/fever → suspect agranulocytosis.”

Medicine 06.question: ৪৫) Husky voice is characteristic of which disease?
Medicine 06.exp:
A husky/hoarse voice is a classic feature of hypothyroidism. It occurs due to myxedematous changes and edema of the vocal cords, which alters the voice.

  • Hypothyroidism → hoarse/husky voice

  • Hyperthyroidism → usually no characteristic husky voice

  • Addison's disease → hyperpigmentation, weakness, hypotension

  • Cushing's syndrome → features of cortisol excess

Exam pearl:
“Hypothyroidism → husky/hoarse voice.”

Medicine 06.question: ৪৬) Which is not a feature of myxoedema?
Medicine 06.exp:
Myxoedema (adult hypothyroidism) causes a reduced metabolic rate, so patients characteristically have cold intolerance, not heat intolerance.

Typical features include:

  • Hoarseness of voice

  • Periorbital edema

  • Delayed relaxation of deep tendon reflexes, especially the ankle jerk

  • Cold intolerance, weight gain, dry skin, constipation, bradycardia

Exam pearl:
“Hypothyroidism/myxoedema → cold intolerance; hyperthyroidism → heat intolerance.”

Medicine 06.question: ৪৭) Which electrolyte imbalance occurs in hypothyroidism?
Medicine 06.exp:
Hyponatremia is a recognized electrolyte abnormality in hypothyroidism, particularly in severe cases. Reduced free-water clearance can lead to dilutional hyponatremia.

  • Hypothyroidism → Hyponatremia

  • Hypernatremia → not typical

  • Hypokalemia/Hyperkalemia → not characteristic electrolyte abnormalities

Exam pearl:
“Hypothyroidism → Hyponatremia.”

Medicine 06.question: ৪৮) Which is primary cause of hyperparathyroidism?
Medicine 06.exp:
Primary hyperparathyroidism is most commonly caused by a single parathyroid adenoma, resulting in autonomous excess secretion of PTH.

  • Single parathyroid adenoma → commonest cause of primary hyperparathyroidism

  • Chronic renal failure → secondary hyperparathyroidism

  • Malabsorption → secondary hyperparathyroidism

  • Osteomalacia → may cause secondary hyperparathyroidism

Exam pearl:
“Primary hyperparathyroidism → single parathyroid adenoma.”

Medicine 06.question: ৪৯) Which is not a feature of Cushing's syndrome?
Medicine 06.exp:
Husky/hoarse voice is classically associated with hypothyroidism (myxoedema), not Cushing's syndrome.

Typical features of Cushing's syndrome include:

  • Moon face

  • Buffalo hump

  • Pendulous abdomen/central obesity

  • Thin skin, purple striae, proximal muscle weakness

  • Hypertension and glucose intolerance

Exam pearl:
“Husky voice → Hypothyroidism; Moon face + buffalo hump → Cushing's syndrome.”

Medicine 06.question: ৫০) Synacthen test is done for diagnosis of which disease?
Medicine 06.exp:
The Synacthen (ACTH stimulation) test is used to assess adrenal cortical function and is the standard confirmatory test for adrenal insufficiency (Addison's disease).

Principle:
Synthetic ACTH (Synacthen) is administered → normally, the adrenal cortex responds by increasing serum cortisol. In Addison's disease, cortisol shows an inadequate rise.

  • Addison's disease → Synacthen test

  • Cushing's syndrome → dexamethasone suppression test

  • Conn's syndrome → aldosterone-renin ratio
